title: Connect observability events to SRE ops workflow: PD/Slack hooks, runbook templating, and postmortem bootstraps
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our alerting and tracing signals currently arrive as separate artifacts (logs, metrics, traces) and require manual enrichment during incidents. On-call SREs spend time copying links and building a postmortem skeleton while context is still fresh. We need an integrated incident-response pipeline that auto-enriches PagerDuty and Slack notifications with trace+trace-span links, SLO snapshot, relevant dashboard links, and creates a draft postmortem (Confluence page or GitHub issue) pre-populated with key telemetry and a runbook checklist.

Scope:
- Add enrichment hooks to the observability backend so alerts and traces share a deterministic request_id and quick links.
- Implement PagerDuty payload enhancements (custom_details) to include: top error traces, sample span id, afflicted model/service, approximate impacted QPS, and link to latency/error dashboard with applied filters.
- Implement a Slack incident channel message template that includes one-click links to the trace flamegraph, log search with built-in filters, and runbook quick actions (acknowledge, escalate, create postmortem).
- Template-driven runbook creation: when an alert reaches severity threshold or PD incident is acknowledged, create a draft postmortem in Confluence or GitHub with prefilled fields (incident timeline header, telemetry snapshot, initial triage notes).
- Add a lightweight automation to populate postmortem with a minimal causality checklist and SLO regression snippet.
- Provide configuration knobs for teams to opt-in/out and to map PD services to runbook templates.

Out of scope for this ticket: full natural-language incident summarization and automated root-cause resolution (RCA) writing. Those will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: PagerDuty incidents created from observability alerts include custom_details linking to: top error trace, sample span ID, relevant latency/error dashboard filtered to the incident time window.
Slack incident notification uses the new template and presents runbook quick actions and direct links to trace and logs for the same request_id.

When an incident is acknowledged (or a PD incident marked 'major'), a draft postmortem is auto-created in the configured workspace (Confluence or GitHub) with the incident header, telemetry snapshot (SLOs, error rate, 95th latency), and a runbook checklist.
Teams can configure PD service -> runbook template mappings via a small UI in the Console or via a config file; default behavior is off and must be enabled for each team.
Added telemetry (metrics + trace link) is validated against staging incidents and test harness with synthetic traces; unit/integration tests cover payload generation and template population.
Documentation exists in Confluence and README with rollout steps and rollback plan.
Security review completed for PD/Slack payload content (no customer PII) and KMS keys used for any API secrets are validated.
Monitoring/alerts created for failures in the automation (failed webhook calls, draft creation errors) and dashboards for adoption metrics (incidents auto-bootstrapped per week).
